title: Predictive memory guardrails: dynamic buffer sizing for weights, KV, and activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe intermittent OOMs and tail latency spikes in high-concurrency hosted tenants during sustained continuous-batching scenarios. Root cause analysis points to overlapping peak demands from weights (model parameters/quantized pages), KV cache growth from long conversations, and transient activation surges during batched long-context requests. Existing static soft-watermarks and simple eviction heuristics either sacrifice throughput or trigger noisy preemption.

Goal: Implement a predictive memory guardrail that dynamically sizes and enforces a small elastic buffer (safety corridor) across three budget buckets: weights (including quantization paging/resident slabs), KV cache (per-tenant and pooled), and activations (runtime ephemeral allocations). The system should: 1) forecast short-horizon memory pressure using recent request traces and batch composition, 2) reserve a predictive headroom corridor that prevents aggressive eviction of weights mid-inference, and 3) expose runtime telemetry and tunable policies for rollout.

Scope: Design, simulator, prototype allocator changes, eviction scoring, and a canary rollout on dedicated clusters. This ticket covers the design doc, simulator runs, API knobs, and a low-risk rollout plan. Implementation will land as follow-ups: allocator integration and eviction policy engine.

acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Eng + Design + PM
Simulator available with representative traces and reproducible runs
Metric definitions and dashboards created: reserved_bytes, pressure_score, eviction_rate, ooms, 99th_latency
Canary rollout plan with conservative/medium/aggressive configurations and clear rollback conditions
decisions: Adopt three-bucket model (weights, KV, activations) rather than single global reserve to avoid protecting the wrong resource.
Forecast horizon: short-term (10s-120s) using EWMA on arrival rate and batch composition; choose percentile-based corridor sizing (e.g., 95th or 99th) per cluster tier.

Eviction scoring must prefer: (1) ephemeral activation compression/early flush, (2) least-recently-used pooled KV shards with grace period, (3) paged quantized weight maps only as last resort to avoid model reload churn.
